instructions.instruction: # Admin Authentication Production Gate

The in-process login throttle is only defense in depth. Serverless instances do not share its memory, so it is not a production rate limit. Login requests derive that local key from the socket peer only; forwarding headers are intentionally ignored because a direct caller can forge them.

The production login endpoint fails closed until `ADMIN_VERCEL_RATE_LIMIT_READY=true` is configured. This is an operator attestation, not evidence that a Vercel Firewall rule exists. Set it only after all of the following are complete for the production project:

3. Publish the Firewall change, then use the Firewall overview for the named rule to confirm the rule is active and observe a controlled test that receives HTTP 429 after the sixth request from one IP.
4. Record the project, rule name, verification time, and operator in the deployment change record. Only then set `ADMIN_VERCEL_RATE_LIMIT_READY=true` in the production environment and redeploy.

Remove the attestation and redeploy before any firewall-rule deletion, project move, route change, or rate-limit-policy change. This immediately disables login until the external control is reverified.

Vercel documents the required Firewall rate-limit workflow, including path conditions, counting keys, publishing changes, and Firewall-overview verification: [WAF Rate Limiting](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/rate-limiting).

- `splitByExpertInsightGate()` blocks long-form memo generation when required fields are empty. Blocked items are converted into source/signal cards with `expertInsightBlocked`, `expertInsightBlockReason`, and missing-field metadata.

- The deterministic fallback body path also starts from the extracted facts, companies, bottleneck, leverage, execution risk, timing dependency, counterargument, and next observable signal so offline generation cannot fall back to generic infrastructure analysis.
- `src/data/latest-news.json`

- `index.astro` combines latest and archived records and calls `buildHomepageFeed(..., { limit: 50, minimumVisible: 30 })`. The limit is an upper bound: a zero or undersized authorized inventory does not manufacture cards.

- `buildHomepageFeed()` admits only an identified record that passes public product fit and current source-text authorization, is not explicitly hidden, archive-only, quarantined, or `archive_only_noindex`, and has not been marked `homepagePublished: false`.

- Featured, visual lead, ticker, and feed sections derive from that one gated feed. Retained JSON, `src/data/search-index.json`, and the `LATEST_NEWS_LIMIT` store split are not independent homepage-publication paths.

Article detail pages are generated by `src/pages/news/[id].astro` from the same combined stores only when `isPublicLongformArticle()` passes: an ID, explicit `articlePagePublished: true`, no signal/brief/archive/quarantine/noindex exclusion, public product fit, detail-quality eligibility, and current source-text authorization are all required.

RSS generation is in `src/pages/rss.xml.ts`. `buildRssItems()` combines latest and archived records, then requires an ID, publication date, `rssItemEligible()` (core or adjacent public route with no noindex/archive exclusion), and current source-text authorization before sorting by analysis/publish time and retaining at most 100 items. - Splits the newest homepage-eligible `LATEST_NEWS_LIMIT` records into `latest`.
- Moves overflow records plus `archiveOnly` / `homepagePublished: false` records into archive, merged with prior archive.
- Converts latest and archive records into searchable records via `toSearchableArticle()`.

`src/data/latest-news.json` is written by `scripts/pipeline.mjs` after `syncArchiveArtifacts()` returns the current latest set.
## 8. Publish/Deploy Hooks
Scheduled publish path:
- It runs `npm run check`, `npm run pipeline`, taxonomy regeneration, `npm test`, and `npm run content:gate`; the content gate performs the production build.
- `src/data/latest-news.json`
- `scripts/state/pipeline-state.json`
Build/deploy path:
- `vercel.json` declares Astro, `npm run build`, and output directory `dist`.

- `package.json` build script runs `prepare:static-images` and `astro build`.

## Production Verification

`VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` is a deployment trigger, not a cache-purge endpoint; do not use it for purge runs.

Pipeline commits to `main` must NOT carry `[skip ci]` in the message: Vercel honors that marker and skips the production deployment, which leaves refreshed articles and authored columns committed to the repository but never published to the live site. GitHub Actions noise is prevented by triggers instead (visual-qa runs on pull requests only; the release job skips bot actors).

Intake health: only sources whose registry entry carries an approved `text_use_basis` (plus a valid `terms_url` and a `reviewed_at` within the review window) are fetched at all — `activeRegistryFeeds()` in `scripts/lib/source-registry.mjs` is the gate. If columns start reporting `no_qualifying_story` run after run, check how many feeds that function returns before suspecting the engine: with a single authorized source the pool drains within days. Add rights-clean sources (US federal public domain, CC BY) to `config/sourceRegistry.yml` rather than weakening the gate.

Relevance scores come from the article's own words (title, snippet, body, source name and URL). The registry `defaultCategory` is a routing hint, never scoring input — folding the label into the text once made every item from an `AI Infrastructure (GPU/Neocloud)` source read as a full memo before a word of it was fetched. When adding a source, verify a few of its items with `Feed Probe` (`feed-probe.yml`, input `urls`) first: it prints HTTP status, content type, and item counts from a GitHub-hosted runner, which is the only place feed URLs can be checked from restricted environments.

Pool composition: `selectPoolItems` keeps only items newer than `POOL_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (10) when anything fresh exists, caps each source at `MAX_ITEMS_PER_SOURCE_IN_POOL` (6), and orders by fetch-time relevance with recency breaking ties. A feed that exposes months of history (NRC ships 165 items) otherwise fills the 30-slot pool with stale notices. The wire publishes at most `ITEMS_PER_RUN` items per KST slot; a verification run outside the schedule needs `force_wire=true` on the `Update News` dispatch (sets `PIPELINE_FORCE_SLOT=1`), otherwise a slot that already ran picks nothing.

Extraction artifacts: every public gate (`currentSourceTextAuthorization`, `publicProductFitResult`, detail-route eligibility) validates `extraction_artifact` through `validateExtractionArtifact`, which requires `extraction_qa.public_publishable === true`, an empty `block_reasons` list, and a sentence-completion score of at least 0.92. `enrichContent` therefore builds the artifact with `analyzeSourceExtractionFailClosed` (the same policy the tier router and homepage filter use), and the pipeline rebuilds older artifacts that predate the flag from the stored source text on every run. An artifact built from raw quality metrics alone is never publishable, which is how the public surface froze on the pinned inventory between August 12 and September 3 while the pipeline kept committing records.

For live production checks from restricted environments, dispatch the `Prod Smoke` workflow (`prod-smoke.yml`) — it probes the homepage, column surfaces, RSS, and sitemap from a GitHub-hosted runner and prints status codes plus content markers into the job log.

EIA restoration step: `restore-eia-public-inventory.mjs` re-fetches the fifteen EIA articles on every run and rebuilds their records from the live text. When EIA serves a truncated or error page (a 146-character "article" failed run #3182 on 2026-09-05), `resolveSourceTexts` retries once and then reuses the text stored in the committed inventory, but only when that record's extraction artifact validates (hash match, same source URL, ≥500 characters); the log line `[restore-eia] <id>: live extraction too short (n); reusing verified text from the committed inventory` records the substitution. With no verified stored text the step still fails closed, so a first-time restoration cannot be faked from a bad fetch.

instructions.instruction: # AI News Portal QA/QC Runbook
This runbook defines the reusable QA/QC gate for the `ai-news-portal` repository and the Compute Current public product surface.
QA/QC covers three simultaneous questions:
- Release readiness: whether the current branch is safe to deploy.
- Reusable quality system: whether future runs can repeat the same checks without relying on private operational credentials.
- `deployable`: local gates pass, merge/data integrity passes, local distribution passes, live verification passes, and no secret-gated operational follow-up remains.

- `deployable with operational follow-up`: local gates pass, merge/data integrity passes, and the built local artifact passes, but live deployment, staging, or cache freshness still needs operator action.
- `blocked`: local gates fail, merge/data integrity fails, or local distribution verification fails.
Run:
npm run qa:qc
The command composes:
- `npm run content:gate`
- JSON parse checks for `src/data/latest-news.json`, `src/data/archived-news.json`, and `src/data/search-index.json`
- production-surface verification against the local `dist` artifact and optional live URL

`--skip-content-gate` is only for reusing a separately captured local-gate result during iterative QA. A skipped content gate is reported as `skipped`, adds an operational follow-up, and must not be treated as an unconditional release pass.
- Do not require production secrets.
- Do not execute cache purge.
- Do not weaken extraction QA, repetition checks, source-fidelity checks, public-content gates, or product-fit boundaries.

Cache purge status must be recorded as an operational follow-up unless a separate operator run explicitly supplies credentials and authorizes purge with an explicit opt-in flag such as `--purge-cache`.
## Merge Audit Checklist
## Release Checklist
1. Run `npm run qa:qc`.
2. Confirm the report verdict is not `blocked`.
3. If the verdict is `deployable with operational follow-up`, verify the follow-up list is limited to deployment, staging, live freshness, or cache status.
4. Commit local docs/scripts/tests/data changes after verification.
5. Push or deploy only after a separate explicit instruction.

instructions.instruction: ## Production Body Path
The deployed article page renders `expertLensFull.finalArticleBody` first, then falls back to `articleText`, `snippet`, and `summary` in `src/pages/news/[id].astro`.
Current production generation path before this change:
1. `scripts/pipeline.mjs` selects publishable crawled items after extraction QA, relevance routing, taxonomy, and expert-insight gates.
3. `generateExpertLensFull()` asks the model for a structured expert-lens JSON payload.

5. If the model output is too short, misses the blueprint, misses expert-insight usage, or contains template language, `finalArticleBody()` falls back to `blueprintFallbackBody()` in `scripts/lib/article-blueprints.mjs`.
6. `blueprintFallbackBody()` previously pulled reusable paragraphs from `buildHumanizedArticleBody()` in `scripts/lib/editorial-humanizer.mjs`.
That means the production body function actually used under failure or fallback conditions was:
- fallback: `scripts/lib/article-blueprints.mjs` -> `blueprintFallbackBody()`
## Expert Blog OS Status

No repository symbol, import, script, or runtime path named `Expert Blog OS`, `expert blog os`, or `blog os` was found. The production path is the `expert-lens` pipeline above, plus the archive/search artifact sync. The new Expert Blog OS pipeline was therefore not actually called before publishing by any identifiable repo path.

| `scripts/lib/editorial-humanizer.mjs` | Production generation code / fallback paragraph bank | Contained repeated opening hooks, audience scaffolds, timing paragraphs, and fallback theses that could be reused unchanged across many articles. |
| `scripts/lib/repetition-detector.mjs` | Publishing gate code | Contained a hardcoded banned phrase list, separate from editorial config. |
| `scripts/test-repetition-detector.mjs` | Test fixture | Contained a literal banned phrase in a repetition detector fixture. |
| `src/data/latest-news.json` | Cached generated articles / static production data | Contained repeated hooks, repeated Editor's Brief lines, and generic infrastructure paragraphs. |
| `src/data/search-index.json` | Cached generated articles / search JSON store | Contained repeated hooks and body copy copied from latest/archive records. |

- Production code and prompt-like fallback surfaces: `scripts/lib/editorial-humanizer.mjs`, `scripts/lib/repetition-detector.mjs`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/lib/AGENTS.override.md`, and one repetition test fixture.
- Cached generated records: `src/data/latest-news.json`, `src/data/archived-news.json`, and `src/data/search-index.json`.

The largest production risk was not the prompt alone. It was the fallback path that reused deterministic body paragraphs whenever model output failed validation, plus the cached JSON artifacts that had already stored those paragraphs.
## Remediation Implemented
- Production fallback article bodies now route through NarrativeDNA generation instead of reusable paragraph banks.
- Publishing gates now load banned phrases from config and block any generated draft containing a banned phrase.

instructions.instruction: - Extraction QA is a publish gate. A source that fails extraction QA may remain a signal item that links to the source, but it must not receive a generated long-form local article.

- Every generated article must carry a source-specific thesis. Avoid broad AI market framing unless the source is directly about infrastructure capacity, power, chips, cloud deployment, data centers, cooling, financing, or policy constraints.
- Run repetition and source-fidelity evals before publishing or marking generated article copy as publishable.
## Prompt and Fallback Copy Rules
- Do not add fallback language that can be reused unchanged across many articles.

- Do not use banned generic patterns in generated or fallback article bodies. The canonical phrase inventory lives in `../../config/bannedPhrases.yml`; do not duplicate blocked strings in prompts, fallback copy, or fixture data unless a test is explicitly asserting the guard.

Before changing publish readiness or content generation behavior, identify where repetition and source-fidelity are checked. If the checks are missing, document that gap rather than assuming the article is safe to publish.
When implementing future behavior changes in this module, tests or verification should cover:
- extraction QA blocking long-form article generation;
- source fidelity for generated claims;
